body:
Hi @jpparis-orange 

Sorry but I just can't follow what you're trying to do here. I think you're trying to do too much all at once, which means that it is not clear where things are going wrong.

Hello @clintongormley 

The gist recreation creates 2 clusters and a tribe node: everything is ok. Then, I'll change the recreation to exhibit the problems.

In the tribe node start (say after line 38), I add the following line 
-Des.cluster.name="T1" \
The tribe node will not connect to the clusters.
Same with -Des.cluster.name="elasticsearch" \

The second problem is about setting transport port. Starting with the recreation, add the following line after line 38
-Des.transport.tcp.port="9900" \
The tribe node will not start.
Same with -Des.transport.tcp.port="9300" \

OK - to make this easier to follow, start two clusters as follows:

```
./bin/elasticsearch --cluster.name C1 --node.name N1 -d
./bin/elasticsearch --cluster.name C2 --node.name N2 -d
```

Then start a tribe node as follows:

```
./bin/elasticsearch --tribe.t1.cluster.name C1 --tribe.t2.cluster.name C2 --node-name T1
```

This works, however doing: `GET localhost:9202/_cluster/state?pretty` will return a cluster name of `elasticsearch`, and this cannot be changed, eg:

```
./bin/elasticsearch --tribe.t1.cluster.name C1 --tribe.t2.cluster.name C2 --node-name T1 --cluster.name foo  # tribe node doesn't join the other cluster
```

Also, trying to set a different transport port for the tribe node doesn't work, eg:

```
./bin/elasticsearch --tribe.t1.cluster.name C1 --tribe.t2.cluster.name C2 --node-name T1 --transport.tcp.port 9900
```

The above fails with:

```
{1.4.2}: Startup Failed ...
- BindTransportException[Failed to bind to [9900]]
    ChannelException[Failed to bind to: 0.0.0.0/0.0.0.0:9900]
        BindException[Address already in use]
```

That's simpler, and it's what I had in mind: sorry for the complicated recreation. Do you want that I simplify the gist too?

Two complements: 
1. --cluster.name elasticsearch give the same result as --cluster.name foo
2. --transport.tcp.port 9300 give the same result as --transport.tcp.port 9900

issue.title: System properties and configuration settings must not be forwarded to tribe clients

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
The tribe node, at startup, sets up the tribe clients that will join their corresponding tribes. All of the tribe.\* settings are properly forwarded to the corresponding tribe client. System properties and global configuration settings (all but tribe.*) must not be forwarded to the tribe clients though or they will end up overriding per tribe settings with same name.

For instance if you set the `transport.tcp.port` to some defined value for the tribe node, via system property or configuration file, that same value must not be forwarded to the tribe clients, otherwise they will try and use the same port, which will be already occupied by the tribe node itself, resulting in startup failed. Same for cluster.name, which will cause the tribe clients not to join their tribes.

This change is quite hard to test in our test infra, given that we make sure that the internal test cluster ignores any system property for proper test isolation. I tested it manually and verfied that the fix works and doesn't seem to have any downside. If anybody has any idea on how we can test this, I would be happy to add some tests to make sure we have proper coverage for it.

Closes #9576
